questions.key_step: Write x^2 as (x^2-4)+4 to get e^x(h+h') form, then use point and slope of tangency.
questions.justification: Standard e^x[f+f'] integral followed by one tangency condition; three routine steps, no insight beyond a well-practised trick. Same standard as a linear-DE/integral SCQ at L2.

questions.key_step: 1^inf form: need the x^6 terms of e^x ln(1+x)+e^-x ln(1-x) because the x^4 term cancels.
questions.justification: The cancellation of x^4 forces a long series expansion to x^6 and a careful ratio; option-based so checkable, but a slip in the x^6 coefficient is easy.

questions.key_step: Family of lines passes through the centroid, and the orthocentre of the right triangle is the right-angle vertex.
questions.justification: Fixed point of a concurrent family and max distance = HG; a short routine chain with one recognised fact.

questions.key_step: Tangent condition gives a=g(t); number of tangents = number of roots of g(t)=a, so analyse monotonicity of g.
questions.justification: Needs the parametrisation, the derivative of g, behaviour near the asymptote t=e and counting of roots for every a; options help.

questions.key_step: y^2=x^3 from the DE; then each statement is a short slope, area or angle calculation.
questions.justification: Four statements each routine (separable DE, slopes, tan of angle, area); multi-concept so the 2.5 floor applies.

questions.key_step: Build f = min(max, max) piecewise: find the crossings (one is root of a quartic), then check slopes at five breakpoints.
questions.justification: Long casework with five breakpoints, one found only as a quartic root, plus maximum and monotonicity statements; one slip changes the count.

questions.key_step: Compute P(E1)=1/2, then test independence of E1 with B and E2 and the conditional probabilities.
questions.justification: Four statements each need a genuine probability computation; independence of E1 and E2 is non-obvious.

questions.key_step: Use sum k x^k and sum k^2 x^k (AGP) for mean and variance; tail-sum formula for statement (C).
questions.justification: Series summations plus a distribution-identity statement; several concepts so the floor applies but the level is 3 anyway.

questions.key_step: g(x)=k(x) for x>=2 since k is increasing there; then (2x-1)(x-2)^2 factorisation.
questions.justification: Understanding max/min over a moving interval needs thought, but once g near 2 is seen the limit is quick.

questions.key_step: Piecewise g with the breakpoint x=1/2 (where k(1/2)=k(2)=4), then F piecewise and its maximum.
questions.justification: Same paragraph but the whole piecewise structure of g must be derived (breakpoint k(x)=4), then F analysed on two pieces.

questions.key_step: Substitute x^3=t, integrate t e^t, then match series terms.
questions.justification: Substitution, boundary condition and a series limit; routine chain.

questions.key_step: Between the lines the product (x-y+2)(x-y-4) is negative; d3^2 = d1 d2 gives a circle.
questions.justification: Distance formulas and sign handling, then circle radius; routine.
questions.nearest_anchor: 2021-P1-Q9 (L4, harder as it adds a chord)

questions.key_step: Four sub-computations: |cubic| kinks, domain integers of a log expression, a limit and the roots of e^x+x^2-x-1; then the median formula.
questions.justification: Four small tasks from different chapters feed a median; each is routine but the chain is long and root counting needs convexity.

questions.key_step: (f')^2+f f'' = (f f')' and Rolle's theorem on the nine interlacing roots of f f'.
questions.justification: Non-routine but familiar Rolle idea: g=ff' has 9 roots, so g' has 8, and degree 8 caps it.

questions.key_step: g is non-differentiable only at 0; h=g(phi(x)) can fail only where phi=0, and one-sided slopes use g'(0-)=1/2, g'(0+)=1.
questions.justification: Inverse of a piecewise function, composition, chain rule with one-sided slopes at three points and a numerical sum; no options.

questions.key_step: f'=0 reduces to 2x^3-6x=k; two local minima exactly when the cubic has three roots, |k|<4.
questions.justification: Reduction to a cubic with local extrema +-4 and care at the boundary |k|=4; a short chain with one subtle edge.

questions.key_step: Parametrise B(t,t), C(s,-s), use AB.AC=0 and eliminate to find the midpoint line.
questions.justification: Parametrisation, dot product and elimination, then a distance; routine chain.
